reason: The hypothesis relies on E1 for the SCCP mechanism's effect on mechanical properties, but E1 does not address thermal conductivity. E2 and E3 provide background on candidate alloys but contain no evidence on thermal conductivity enhancement or the effect of nanoprecipitates on heat transfer. The key premise that coherent nanoprecipitates improve thermal conductivity is entirely unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: SCCPs form coherent nanoprecipitates that relieve stress concentrations and facilitate dislocation transmission, enhancing ductility and strength in tungsten RHEAs.
Refractory high-entropy alloys (CrFeTiTa)70W30 and VFeTiTaW can be produced by mechanical alloying and sintering and are candidates for interlayers.
Coherent nanoprecipitates can act as micro-scale thermal bridges to increase thermal conductivity via improved electron/phonon coupling.
The SCCP heat treatment can be applied to the specific interlayer alloys (e.g., CrFeTiTa-based or VFeTiTaW) to induce beneficial nanoprecipitates.
The predicted outcome (≥10% thermal conductivity increase with maintained mechanical integrity) is achievable under plasma-facing conditions up to 800 °C.
